main_text: 11.2. DE QVAESTIONIBUS SECVNDI SVBIECTI. QVOD EST ANGELVS 71. Quaeritur: Vtrum angeli sint? Et respondendum est, quod sic. Si enim illud, quod uidetur minus esse, simile Deo est, et multo magis id, quod maius uidetur esse, simile Deo est. Adhuc: Si aliquod compositum ex corporali et intellectuali est, multo magis id, quod est compositum ex intellectuali et intellectuali, est. Amplius: Si angeli quidem non essent, scala differentiae et concordantiae esset euacuata, et per consequens mundus; quod est impossibile. 72. Quaeritur: Angelus de quo est, et cuius est? Et respondendum est per regulam D, quod est de se ipso; sua enim essentia non potest esse punctualis neque linealis. Et per secundam speciem eiusdem regulae est de suis correlatiuis spiritualibus, scilicet de suis -tiuis et -bilibus et -are, ex quibus est compositus. Per -tiuos est actiuus, per -bile est receptiuus, et -are est actus, existens intra -tiuos et -biles. Per tertiam speciem est dicendum, quod angelus est Dei. Et haec de angelis sufficiant causa breuitatis. 11.3. DE QVAESTIONIBVS TERTII SVBIECTI QVOD EST CAELVM 73. Vtrum caelum moueat se ipsum? Et respondendum est quod sic, ut sua principia habeant correlatiuos substantiales et proprios per suas constellationes. 74. Vtrum caelum moueat se ad locum? Et respondendum est, quod sic, in se et in inferioribus circulariter, sed non extra se. Ratio huius est, quia extra se nullam actionem habet uel habere potest. 75. Vtrum angelus moueat caelum? Et respondendum est, quod non; quia si moueret, iam -tiui suorum correlatiuorum essent inferius, et -biles superius; et etiam per suam formam iam non moueret elementa nec elementata, sed per suam materiam; quod est impossibile. 76. Quaeritur: Vtrum caelum habeat animam motiuam? Et respondendum est, quod sic. Nam aliter sensitiua et uegetatiua non haberent animas motiuas, nec elementa haberent motum. 77. Quaeritur per primam speciem regulae de E: Quare est caelum? Et dicendum est, quod ex eo, quia ex sua forma et materia est constitutum. 78. Per secundam speciem regulae E quaeritur: Caelum quare est? Et respondendum est, ut entia inferiora possint habere motum. Et haec de caelo sufficiant causa breuitatis.

ALPHABET_D_E.text: D significat aeternitatem siue durationem, contrarietatem, de quo, caelum, fortitudinem et luxuriam. E significat potestatem, principium, quare, hominem, temperantiam et superbiam.

RULES_3_4.text: 3. Regula 'De quo' habet tres species. Prima est primitiua; sicut quando dicitur: Intellectus de quo est? Et est respondendum, quod est de se ipso, eo quia non deriuatur ab aliquo generali naturaliter. Secunda species est, quando quaeritur specialiter: De quo est ens? Sicut quando quaeritur: De quo est intellectus? Et est respondendum, quod est de sua forma et sua materia specificis, cum quibus habet specificum intelligere. Tertia species est, quando quaeritur: Cuius est ens? Sicut quando quaeritur: Cuius est intellectus? Et est respondendum, quod est hominis, sicut pars sui totius, et equus sui domini. 4. Quarta regula habet duas species, scilicet formalem et finalem. Formalis, quando quaeritur: Ens quare est? Sicut quando quaeritur: Intellectus quare est? Et est respondendum, quod est de sua forma et de sua materia specificis, cum quibus habet specificum intelligere, et cum ipsis agit per suam speciem. Secunda species est respectu finis. Sicut quando quaeritur: Intellectus quare est? Et respondendum est: Vt sint obiecta intelligibilia; aut ut de rebus scientia haberi possit.

SUBJECTS_ANGEL_HEAVEN.text: 2 DE SECVNDO SVBIECTO. QVOD EST DE ANGELO Angelus est deducibilis per principia et regulas. Ipse quidem naturalem bonitatem, magnitudinem, durationem habet, etc. Et definitur sic: Angelus est spiritus, corpori non coniunctus. In ipso non est contrarietas naturalis, nam incorruptibilis est. In ipso est materia de -bilibus, scilicet de bonificabili et magnificabili, etc., ut per secundam speciem D significatum est. In angelo est maioritas, eo quia est magis similis Deo, quam homo; quia altiora principia et regulas habet, quam homo. Et in isto passu cognoscit intellectus, quod si homo non potest uti sensibilibus absque organis, non sequitur propter hoc, quod angelus non possit sine organo; nam angelus natura est superior. Et in isto passu cognoscit intellectus, quod angeli possunt loqui inter se et agere in nobis absque organo, et transire ab uno loco ad alium sine medio; et sic de aliis, ut patet per intellectum, discursum per regulas. In angelo est differentia. Nam suus intellectus, uoluntas et memoria differentes sunt inter se. Aequalitas intelligendi, amandi et recolendi est in angelo, ratione obiecti supremi, ut Deus, qui aequaliter est intelligibilis, amabilis et recolibilis. In angelo est minoritas; nam ex nihilo ipse est creatus. 3 DE TERTIO SVBIECTO. QVOD EST DE CAELO Caelum habet bonitatem naturalem, magnitudinem et durationem, etc. Et definitur sic: Caelum est prima substantia mobilis. In eo non est contrarietas. Non enim est ex principiis contrariis compositum. In ipso enim sunt instinctus et appetitus naturales, et per consequens motus, sine quo non posset habere naturam, instinctum et appetitum. Verumtamen in eo est principium. Efficiens enim est in inferioribus; et etiam est constitutum ex sua forma et materia specifica, ut agat per suam speciem. Suus motus est ei finis et quies. Caelum est in suo loco, sicut corpus in sua superficie. Adhuc est in tempore. Ipsum namque nouum est, et est etiam in tempore, sicut efficiens in suo effectu. Et sic de aliis suis accidentibus suo modo.

Q80_BOUNDARY_WARNING.text: 80. Quaeritur: Quare homo agit per formam specificam? Vade ad secundam speciem regulae E, et ibi est solutio implicata.

COLOPHON.text: DE FINE HVIVS ARTIS Ad honorem et laudem Dei et publicae utilitatis finiuit Raimundus hunc librum Pisis in monasterio sancti Domnini, mense Ianuarii anno Domini 1307 incarnationis Domini nostri Iesu Christi. Amen.

all_written_reasons: A comparative God-likeness argument; preserve ALIM punctuation, which the comparison edition disputes.
If a bodily-and-intellectual composite exists, all the more an intellectual-and-intellectual composite exists.
Without angels the ladder of difference and concordance, and consequently the world, would be emptied, which the source rejects as impossible.
complete_question_inventory.limits: These are the source’s metaphysical arguments, not independently demonstrated empirical premises.

complete_question_inventory.question_content: From what, and whose, is an angel?
complete_question_inventory.written_answer: Under rule D: from itself; under its second species: from its spiritual correlatives; under its third: belonging to God.
all_written_reasons: The essence is not point-like or linear.
The written -tiuis / -bilibus / -are supply the correlatives of which it is composed.
Per -tiuos is active, per -bile receptive, -are is the act existing within/between -tiuos and -biles.
complete_question_inventory.limits: De se ipso is the source’s primitive/specification answer, not a claim of temporal self-creation or a physical stock. The actor/receptive/act scheme does not specify every lexical correlative root.

all_written_reasons: So that its principles have substantial and proper correlatives through its constellations.
complete_question_inventory.limits: Keep the constellation phrase; do not replace it by an invented mechanical actuator.

complete_question_inventory.question_content: Whether heaven moves itself to a place.
complete_question_inventory.written_answer: Affirmative in itself and in inferior things circularly, but not outside itself.
all_written_reasons: Outside itself it has, or can have, no action.
complete_question_inventory.limits: The coexistence of in inferioribus and non extra se is retained; it is not converted into an unambiguous modern trajectory or spatial containment theorem.

all_written_reasons: If it did, the -tiui of its correlatives would be below and -biles above.
It would then move elements and elemented things by its matter rather than by its form; this is called impossible.
complete_question_inventory.limits: The exact possessor in suorum and suam is not independently settled here. The source asserts the counterfactual reversal; the suffix rule alone does not prove that physical/metaphysical implication.

complete_question_inventory.question_content: Whether heaven has a motive soul.
all_written_reasons: Otherwise the sensitive and vegetative would have no motive souls, and elements no movement.
complete_question_inventory.limits: This is a dependency asserted by the source, not a current natural-scientific law.

complete_question_inventory.question_content: Under the first species of rule E: why does heaven exist?
complete_question_inventory.written_answer: Because it is constituted of its form and matter.
all_written_reasons: The first-species context selects the formal/constitutive answer category.
complete_question_inventory.limits: No numerical material portions or workshop mixture are implied.

complete_question_inventory.question_content: Under the second species of rule E: why does heaven exist?
complete_question_inventory.written_answer: So that inferior beings can have motion.
all_written_reasons: The second-species context selects the final/purpose answer category.
complete_question_inventory.limits: The closing Et haec de caelo sufficiant causa breuitatis remains owned; it is not an extra motion instruction.

D_rule_species.2: specific constituents, form/matter and spiritual correlatives

critical_limits: Leading hyphens are the owned modern transcription’s notation; no diplomatic medieval graphic claim.
The actual whole passage uses ordinary Latin prose plus letters, subtype references and correlative abbreviations. The five role classes are not an encoding of all its content.

Alphabet D also denotes duration, contrariety, heaven, fortitude and luxury; E also denotes power, principle, human, temperance and pride. Explicit rule context selects the interrogative family; the rule species selects within it. Neither D nor E alone chooses every interpretation.
ALIM’s full alphabet has the previously reported missing C sentence; it is not repaired from the comparison text. This packet uses the complete D/E sentences only.
The comparison edition’s rule headers use alphabetic labels where ALIM numbers3/4. Actual D/E references in questions72/77/78 are nevertheless printed in ALIM itself.
Comparison edition note17 disputes punctuation in question71’s first argument. Own ALIM punctuation; do not claim a uniquely parsed existence proof.

Question80 separately refers the why-specific-form question to the second species of E without giving its answer. Retain as a boundary warning against deciding every species from the noun form alone; no silent correction or universal classifier is inferred.
Primitive de se ipso and created-from-nothing in the prerequisite angel account are not flattened into one temporal-origin predicate.
The source’s theology and cosmology constrain its declared content, not an empirical truth test.
